protections: _UnsafeExtensionError.ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS (yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py:5118-5220) plus sanitize_extension (5227-5241): an extension value is accepted only if the text after its last dot is in the allowlist (unless prepend=True) and it contains no slash or backslash.

replace_extension/prepend_extension (_utils.py:2142-2155) are the only public helpers that turn an extension value into a filename suffix, so every name-building call site is meant to route through the same allowlist.
_catch_unsafe_extension_error (yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py:186-197) wraps process_info (3315) and _prepare_filename (1510) so a refusal aborts the file instead of writing it to disk.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The extension comes from the extractor's own format selection rather than from the user or a link, and the obvious attacker-controlled variant (a direct link) is already guarded at extractor/generic.py:907, so %(ext)s reads as trusted metadata.

Loading a local JSON file is an explicit advanced user choice (the file is 'created with --write-info-json', README.md:716), and the loader already carries a safeguard against old/insecure infojson for headers (2966-2969), so it reads as a trusted legacy path.
correct_ext only runs when separate video and audio formats are merged and the extension is then rewritten by ffmpeg, so it reads as an unsupported combination rather than a file-creation sink.

It is the feature itself: the four shortcut options are documented to produce .url/.desktop/.webloc (YoutubeDL.py:314-318, options.py:1597-1600), so refusing those suffixes is a regression, not a fix.

It is a documented opt-out (README.md:2354) that deliberately replaces the sanitiser with an identity lambda, so the user is understood to have asked for unsafe extensions and the branch looks out of scope by construction.
The extractor package independently re-applies the same ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS test for direct links, so that route already looks guarded and the report never names a second package.

The table is a flat hand-maintained list of legitimate download formats, and asx/m3u/svg/mhtml/swf are produced by real features, so a report naming .desktop/.url/.webloc does not ask for them to be dropped.
Subtitle and thumbnail extensions come from the extractor's own URLs and are already passed through replace_extension, so they read as sanitised.

The value is only an infix before the preserved real suffix, so it can never be the OS-interpreted final extension, and test/test_utils.py:318-323 explicitly requires an unlisted infix ('exe') to be accepted.
The CLI exposes exactly the three shortcut types, so a literal exemption list is behaviourally identical today and looks simpler than deriving it from LINK_TEMPLATES.

masking: Fixing T1 makes T5 visible: deleting url/desktop/webloc from ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS makes _write_link_file raise at YoutubeDL.py:3398, and the _catch_unsafe_extension_error wrapper on process_info (186-197, applied at 3315) turns that into report_error -> DownloadError (1094-1100), so --write-link only stops working after the allowlist is fixed.

Fixing T1 promotes T2/T3 to the only remaining routes to an OS-interpreted suffix, because the table edit cannot reach the %(ext)s substitution at YoutubeDL.py:1511-1536 or the --load-info-json ingress at 3693-3702.

conflicts.what: Deleting desktop/url/webloc from ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS makes replace_extension raise at YoutubeDL.py:3398, so --write-link/--write-url-link/--write-webloc-link/--write-desktop-link (LINK_TEMPLATES at _utils.py:4618-4622) stop producing files and the whole video aborts through process_info (3315, 1094-1100); the exemption has to be per call site, not global.

Threading a new _allowed_exts keyword through sanitize_extension breaks the documented --compat-options allow-unsafe-ext monkeypatch `lambda x, prepend=False: x` (__init__.py:622) with a TypeError on every name-building call, including for users who explicitly opted out (README.md:2354).

Extending the allowlist test into the prepend branch, the obvious 'sanitise every component' move, makes the 'f{format_id}' infixes at YoutubeDL.py:3504-3506 and 3537-3539 raise and contradicts test/test_utils.py:318-323, which requires the unlisted infix 'exe' to be accepted.

fairness_risks: The internet-shortcut feature must keep writing .url/.desktop/.webloc (docstring YoutubeDL.py:314-318, options.py:1597-1600, LINK_TEMPLATES _utils.py:4618-4622); any rule that refuses those suffixes outright contradicts a documented feature.

--compat-options allow-unsafe-ext (README.md:2354, __init__.py:618-622) must keep accepting any extension, so sanitize_extension's signature and call convention cannot change without updating the monkeypatch.

Prepend infixes must stay unchecked (test/test_utils.py:318-323 and the f{format_id} callers at YoutubeDL.py:3504-3506/3537-3539); a blanket 'check every dotted component' rule breaks existing tests and every multi-format download.

Legitimate non-media outputs live in the same table: svg thumbnails (_utils.py:5190), mhtml storyboards (5101, 5213), m3u manifests (5216) and xml annotations via OUTTMPL_TYPES (_utils.py:2868, 5209); tightening the policy to every browser/OS-interpreted type removes them.
--load-info-json is a documented workflow (README.md:716) fed by --write-info-json, so a load-time policy must still accept everything the writer emits (4376-4393).

The 'bin' remap and the deliberately allowed 'unknown_video' entry (_utils.py:5127, 5236-5237) mean an extension-less or remapped value must remain acceptable; a rule requiring a real media type breaks that fallback.

design.why: The report leads to the allowlist table (_utils.py:5118) and the published fix is a data edit plus a per-call-site override, which leaves five independent judgements across three files. T1 is the named policy bug (easy for both models). T2 is a sink the table edit cannot reach at all: the default %(ext)s template substitutes info_dict['ext'] straight into the filename and replace_extension is only consulted when final_ext or a forced OUTTMPL_TYPE is set (1511-1536), with a strong 'trusted extractor metadata' dismissal. T4 is a second raw concatenation in the merge path (3478-3489) that still appends a per-format ext with no sanitisation even if a central check is added, and it has its own 'merge-only, ffmpeg rewrites it' dismissal. T5 forces the fix to be per-call-site instead of a global removal, because process_info is wrapped at 3315 and the link feature is documented at 314-318; getting this wrong aborts --write-link. T6 forces the new keyword to stay compatible with the documented allow-unsafe-ext monkeypatch (__init__.py:622). DeepSeek must notice two absent-protection routes with plausible trusted-input dismissals; MiMo must not over-harden the two coupled values. History: the earlier fix for CVE-2024-38519 (Changelog.md:1713-1718) wrote this very table and whitelisted the three link suffixes so that --write-link would keep working (docstring cites the advisory at _utils.py:5116), so the later bug sits in code the earlier fix wrote: incomplete by design, not a regression, and it cannot be fixed by a dependency bump.

unverified: The fix commit e578e265f7c6ca94a74b30e0d8d6196a4d19fb6a is not present in this worktree and no shell is available, so the claim that the published fix adds an _allowed_exts keyword at _utils.py:2142-2151 and YoutubeDL.py:3398-3400 is taken from the screener record; the pinned code at those lines has no such parameter.
Whether the hidden tests can drive --write-link and --load-info-json fully offline (test/parameters.json only sets writelink/writewebloclink false and test_YoutubeDL.py contains no link-file test).
Whether asx/swf/svg/mhtml/m3u are treated as in-scope OS-interpreted types by the advisory or only the three link suffixes are; T8's tier and independence assume a generic report.

No exhaustive extractor scan was possible, so it is unverified whether any extractor emits a format ext outside ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS that a central check would newly reject (the HLS subtitle path at extractor/common.py:2299-2303 shows ext values are routinely derived from URLs).

Multi-component values whose only checked part is the text after the last dot (sanitize at _utils.py:5234-5235, subtitles_filename at 1321-1322, thumbnails at YoutubeDL.py:4502) were examined and treated as a false lead rather than a trap: with an allowed final component the result is name.<unchecked>.<allowed>, so no OS-interpreted final suffix is created.

The OUTTMPL_TYPES sibling suggested as injection room (_utils.py:2863-2875) was not counted as a trap because every forced extension already flows through replace_extension at YoutubeDL.py:1528 and is therefore covered by the allowlist fix.

Link-file body fields (Name= built from the output filename at YoutubeDL.py:3406-3411, URL= percent-encoded via iri_to_uri) and verbatim subtitle bodies (4451-4456) are content-level concerns outside this extension-policy advisory and were not evaluated as traps.
